title: Which sign goes in each box, without working it out?
description: Four pairs of expressions are compared by looking at the brackets and what each number multiplies. No pair is worked out to a final value.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare two expressions, look at what each outside number multiplies and what the brackets open into, before any value is found. Watch for students who work out every value instead of reasoning.

video_script.why: The child compares two expressions by reasoning about brackets and what each number multiplies.
video_script.substitution: Open each bracket, compare the terms, and decide the sign from what is added or taken away.
video_script.anchor: Four pairs of expressions with a box between them
video_script.payoff_line: The boxes take greater than, less than, less than and equals.

final_answer.spoken: the boxes take greater than, less than, less than and equals

never_show: the final value of any expression
maths_rules: 8 − 3 is positive and 3 − 8 is negative, so (8 − 3) × 29 > (3 − 8) × 29
15 + 9 × 18 < (15 + 9) × 18, because the right side also has 15 × 18
video_script.design: One idea: compare by what each number multiplies and what a bracket opens into. Uses the method of the solved example on adding the rows first. The four pairs stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four pairs of expressions with a box between each pair: (a) (8 − 3) × 29 [ ] (3 − 8) × 29 (b) 15 + 9 × 18 [ ] (15 + 9) × 18 (c) 23 × (17 − 9) [ ] 23 × 17 + 23 × 9 (d) (34 − 28) × 42 [ ] 34 × 42 − 28 × 42

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about comparing expressions.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>Four pairs of expressions have a box between them.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>We fill each box by reasoning, without working out the values. Which sign goes in each box?

beats.on_screen: the four pairs stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a balance with two pans; beside it the words: look at the brackets, look at what each number multiplies

marks.g2: the bracket on one pan opens into its terms
marks.g3: an arrow shows an outside number reaching a term

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>To compare, we look at the terms and the brackets.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>A bracket opens when the outside number multiplies each term.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Then we see which side has more.

beats.on_screen: Given: four pairs of expressions with a box between them

marks.gv1: the four pairs are written with their boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, four pairs of expressions with a box between each pair.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sign in each box, by reasoning

marks.fd1: the words the sign in each box are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find the sign for each box, by reasoning.

beats.on_screen: (a) 8 − 3 is positive, 3 − 8 is negative, same 29 on both sides, so (8 − 3) × 29 > (3 − 8) × 29

marks.s11: the two brackets are placed on a number line, one above zero and one below
marks.s12: the same 29 is shown on both sides
marks.s13: the sign greater than is written in the box

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, the first pair.
Eight minus three is above zero, and three minus eight is below zero.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>Both brackets are multiplied by the same twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='s13'/>The left side is above zero and the right side is below zero. The left side is greater, so the box is greater than.

beats.on_screen: (b) 15 + 9 × 18: the 18 multiplies only the 9; (15 + 9) × 18 = 15 × 18 + 9 × 18: the 18 multiplies both; so <

marks.s21: the 18 is drawn reaching only the 9 on the left
marks.s22: the bracket on the right opens into 15 × 18 + 9 × 18
marks.s23: the sign less than is written in the box

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, the second pair.
On the left, eighteen multiplies only the nine.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>On the right, the bracket opens, and eighteen multiplies the fifteen as well.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>The right side has more, so the box is less than.

marks.s32: the right side shows 23 × 9 added instead of taken away
marks.s33: the sign less than is written in the box

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, the third pair.
The left bracket opens into twenty three times seventeen minus twenty three times nine.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>The right side adds twenty three times nine instead of taking it away.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>Taking away leaves less, so the box is less than.

beats.on_screen: (d) (34 − 28) × 42 = 34 × 42 − 28 × 42, the same as the right side, so =

marks.s42: it matches the right side term by term
marks.s43: the sign equals is written in the box

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, the last pair.
The left bracket opens into thirty four times forty two minus twenty eight times forty two.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>That is exactly the right side.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>The two sides are the same, so the box is equals.

marks.s51: the second pair is tried with small numbers
marks.s52: the third pair is tried with small numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='s51'/>Step five, check two pairs with small numbers.
Two plus three times four is fourteen. Open bracket two plus three close bracket times four is twenty.
<bookmark mark='s52'/>Two times open bracket five minus three close bracket is four. Two times five plus two times three is sixteen.
Both checks agree with our signs.

marks.a1: the four signs are placed in the boxes and the answer is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>The boxes take greater than, less than, less than and equals.
